title: He spent his career as a government bureaucrat. He also became one of India's greatest living poets.

sources.text: Library of Congress, South Asian Literary Recordings Project - Sitakant Mahapatra profile

caption:
He spent his career as a government bureaucrat. He also became one of India's greatest living poets.

Born September 17, 1937 in Odisha, Mahapatra joined the Indian Administrative Service in 1961 and served until his retirement in 1995 - a full career inside the government, running alongside a second career most colleagues never attempted.

Mahapatra won the 1974 Sahitya Akademi Award, then the Jnanpith Award in 1993 - India's highest literary honor. He also spent years researching the tribal oral traditions of Eastern Odisha, work most of his readers never saw.

He received the Padma Bhushan in 2002 and the Padma Vibhushan in 2011 - both for literature, both arriving well after his government career had already ended. A bureaucrat's file doesn't usually outlive his poetry. His did the opposite.
